title: Robustness of Anyonic Time-Domain Interference Against Dephasing
authors: Hai-Dong Li, Hao-Xiang Long, Gu Zhang, D. Y. Xing, Wei Chen
abstract: Recent anyon-collider experiments have identified time-domain braiding (TDB) as a new route to probing anyonic statistics. However, how such time-domain interference responds to environmental noise remains an open question. Here we show that TDB interference is intrinsically more robust than its spatial counterpart. In conventional spatial interference, environmental noise induces phase fluctuations that accumulate throughout all paths, leading to exponential suppression of the interference as the dephasing rate increases. In TDB, by contrast, the interfering temporal paths experience largely overlapping environmental fluctuations, whose contributions cancel out in the relative phase, so that only a small nonoverlapping temporal window contributes to dephasing. As a result, TDB interference decays only algebraically with the dephasing rate, providing a new experimental hallmark for its identification. We propose a Fabry-Perot fractional quantum Hall setup in which both types of interference coexist and experience the same environmental noise, enabling a direct comparison of their dephasing behaviors. Our results establish robustness against dephasing as a fundamental advantage of TDB and suggest new opportunities for exploiting anyonic interference in noisy mesoscopic systems.
summary: This theoretical work compares the environmental robustness of Time-Domain Braiding (TDB) interference against standard spatial interference in fractional quantum Hall systems. The authors demonstrate that TDB interference is fundamentally more robust because the shared environmental noise causes noise contributions to cancel out in the relative phase. This results in a distinct, measurable power-law decay signature for TDB versus the exponential decay seen in spatial interference.
main_problem: The paper investigates how Time-Domain Braiding (TDB) interference compares to conventional spatial interference when subjected to environmental dephasing noise.
main_result: TDB interference exhibits a superior robustness, decaying only algebraically with the dephasing rate, whereas spatial interference suffers exponential suppression.
method: The analysis involves calculating the noise-averaged interference current using the chiral Luttinger liquid description and comparing the resulting decay factors for both interference types.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a Fabry-Pérot fractional quantum Hall geometry featuring three edge channels. The physics is described using the chiral Luttinger liquid theory, incorporating tunneling events at Quantum Point Contacts (QPCs).
key_observables: The primary observables are the noise-averaged interference currents, $I_{TDB}$ and $I_{FP}$, and their respective decay factors ($D_{TDB}$ and $D_{FP}$).
important_parameters: Key parameters include the dephasing rate ($	au_\phi$), the non-overlapping temporal window ($|T|$), and the characteristic length/time scales ($	au_g, 	au_\delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes Gaussian phase fluctuations with short-range correlations and utilizes the chiral Luttinger liquid description for edge states.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the conceptual difference in noise coupling between TDB and spatial interference. Figure 2 shows the proposed FQH interferometer setup where both interference types coexist.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by modeling both spatial and TDB interference in the FQH setup. It then derives the noise-averaged current expectation values, contrasting the exponential decay of spatial interference with the algebraic decay of TDB. Finally, it proposes the FP setup for direct experimental comparison.
why_interesting: The finding that TDB exhibits algebraic decay rather than exponential decay provides a distinct, measurable signature for anyonic physics in realistic, noisy mesoscopic devices, which is highly relevant for quantum sensing and computation.
